questionText: Which of the following elements is the most reliable indicator of a secure, official website?
options: The logo of the organization displayed on the page.
A lock icon in the browser address bar alongside an official verified HTTPS domain.
A banner claiming the site is "Safe and Certified by RBI".
The color scheme matching the company's official branding.
explanation: Visual elements like logos and banners are easily copied by hackers. The only verifiable check is the browser address bar checking for secure HTTPS and a correctly spelled official domain.
learningObjective: Identify verified domains and security indicators.

questionText: You receive an email from "service-support@bank-security-update.in" asking you to click a link to verify your account. What is the safest first step?
options: Click the link and fill out the details quickly to avoid account suspension.
Reply to the email asking if it is legitimate.
Delete the email, and verify independently by visiting the bank's official website directly.
Forward the email to your friends to warn them.
explanation: Never use contacts or links provided in unsolicited security emails. Always go directly to the verified bank URL to check account status.

questionText: How does smishing differ from traditional email phishing?
options: Smishing only targets computer systems, while phishing targets phones.
Smishing is delivered via SMS/text messaging, whereas phishing is delivered via email.
Smishing is completely legal, whereas phishing is a crime.
There is no difference; they are identical.
explanation: Smishing refers to phishing attacks executed over Short Message Service (SMS) text messages, often containing shortened links or mobile numbers.

questionText: Under the Information Technology Act, 2000, what is the maximum imprisonment for identity theft (Section 66C)?
options: Up to 1 year
Up to 3 years
Up to 7 years
Life imprisonment
explanation: Section 66C of the IT Act prescribes imprisonment of up to 3 years and a fine of up to ₹1,00,000 for fraudulent use of another's password or signature.
learningObjective: Know the penalties for electronic identity theft.

questionText: You land on a login page for a banking service. Which of the following warnings indicates the connection is NOT encrypted?
options: A "Connection is secure" notification.
The protocol prefix reads "http://" instead of "https://".
The page has a dark background.
The page is in English.
explanation: HTTP connections are unencrypted, allowing attackers to intercept credentials in plain text. Secure pages always use HTTPS.

questionText: What is "Spear Phishing"?
options: Phishing attacks targeted randomly at millions of users.
A highly targeted phishing attack customized for a specific individual or organization.
A phishing scam that uses voice calls instead of email.
A physical attack on computer servers.
explanation: Spear phishing targets specific individuals or organizations using personalized details (like names, department roles) to appear authentic.

questionText: Myth or Fact: If a website address starts with HTTPS and shows a lock icon, the business/content on the page is guaranteed to be honest and safe.
options: Fact: HTTPS lock certificates are only issued to honest, safe businesses.
Myth: Attackers can easily get free HTTPS certificates to secure their fake login pages.
explanation: HTTPS only guarantees that the connection is encrypted, not that the owner of the page is legitimate. Phishing sites frequently use HTTPS.
learningObjective: Deconstruct the lock icon security myth.

questionText: You receive a Skype message from a coworker asking you to download and review an attached PDF report urgently. The phrasing is slightly off. What should you do?
options: Download and open the document to be helpful.
Ignore the message completely.
Contact the coworker through an alternate trusted channel (like phone or in-person) to verify they sent it.
Reply on Skype asking if they are real.
explanation: Accounts can be hijacked. Always verify unusual requests or files using a separate, out-of-band communication channel.

questionText: If you suspect you have clicked a phishing link and entered your Netbanking password, what should be your FIRST action?
options: Report it to the police cyber cell.
Call your bank immediately to block the accounts and change the compromised password.
Wait 24 hours to see if any money is deducted.
Uninstall the browser.
explanation: Minimize damage by immediately locking your banking credentials and changing your passwords to revoke attacker access.

questionText: What is the safest way to verify an unexpected security alert email from an online service provider?
options: Click the link in the email and see if it looks real.
Call the support phone number listed in the email body.
Navigate to the service official app/website independently, log in, and check for alerts.
Ignore it completely as all security alerts are scams.
explanation: Always inspect and verify notifications independently by logging into your profile directly through official bookmarks or apps.

questionText: What is the primary defining characteristic of "Social Engineering"?
options: Exploiting hardware bugs in computers.
Manipulating human psychology and trust to gain unauthorized access to assets or data.
Writing programs to crawl social media websites.
Designing websites for public institutions.
explanation: Social engineering exploits human qualities like trust, urgency, fear, or curiosity to compromise security, rather than bypassing technical barriers directly.

questionText: You get a call from "Airtel Support" saying your SIM card will be deactivated in 1 hour due to missing KYC. They ask you to install "AnyDesk" to complete KYC. What should you do?
options: Install AnyDesk and let them guide you to keep the SIM card active.
Hang up immediately. Official operators never ask you to install remote control apps.
Provide your Aadhaar number over the call instead.
Give them the contact number of your family members.
explanation: AnyDesk/TeamViewer allow attackers to remotely view your phone screen, bypass MFA, and capture passwords. Never install screen-sharing software for caller requests.

questionText: An SMS claims: "Congratulations! You have won a ₹5,00,000 cash lottery from KBC. Click this link to claim your reward before midnight." Which indicator is most suspicious?
options: The high prize amount.
The urgency (midnight deadline) and the request to click a link to receive money.
The SMS is in English.
The name of the lottery program.
explanation: Urgency combined with free lottery cash claims is a classic baiting vector. Genuine entities do not send link-based cash lotteries.

questionText: A caller claiming to be a CBI officer states you are under "digital arrest" for money laundering via your Aadhaar. They demand you stay on a Skype call and transfer funds to audit. What is your safest response?
options: Transfer the funds to prove your innocence and cooperate.
Hang up immediately. No law enforcement agency has the power of "digital arrest" or demands transfers over calls.
Request them to send a WhatsApp copy of their ID badge first.
Stay on the call but refuse to pay.
explanation: Digital arrest is a complete fraud. Police and government agencies never arrest citizens online, place them on video holds, or solicit escrow audits.

questionText: What is the maximum prison sentence for cheating by personation under Section 66D of the IT Act?
options: Up to 1 year
Up to 3 years
Up to 5 years
Up to 10 years
explanation: Section 66D specifies that cheating by personation using a communication device carries imprisonment of up to 3 years and a fine of up to ₹1,00,000.
learningObjective: Identify criminal penalties for electronic personation.

questionText: Myth or Fact: Social engineering attackers are easy to detect because they sound uneducated, speak rudely, or make obvious spelling mistakes.
options: Fact: Professionals never fall for scams because scammers are transparently clumsy.
Myth: Scammers often speak professionally, use formal templates, and build high trust profiles.
explanation: Modern social engineers use professional scripts, authentic terminology, and clone actual company materials to build trust.
learningObjective: Reconstruct psychological profiles of social engineers.

questionText: A WhatsApp message from your supervisor's real name and picture claims they are in a meeting and need you to purchase 5 Google Play gift cards for a client immediately. What should you do?
options: Buy the gift cards and message the codes to keep your supervisor happy.
Report it to the IT administrator and call the supervisor directly on their cell phone to verify.
Ignore the request and buy only 1 card to be safe.
Ask the supervisor to email you from their personal account.
explanation: This is a classic "Executive Impersonation" spear phishing tactic. Verify requests involving monetary transfers via voice or in-person checks.

questionText: What is the primary difference between vishing and phishing?
options: Vishing is done via telephone/voice, while phishing is done via electronic text/email.
Vishing is legal in corporate setups, while phishing is not.
Vishing targets only mobile SIMs, while phishing targets only servers.
Vishing is an automated bot virus, while phishing is manual.
explanation: Vishing (voice phishing) uses direct telephone calls to manipulate targets, whereas phishing represents the broader category primarily associated with emails/messages.

questionText: During a vishing call, if the caller creates massive panic by claiming your credit card is locked due to fraudulent logs, what should you do FIRST?
options: Give them your OTP immediately to cancel the block.
Hang up immediately, wait 3 minutes, and call the official support number printed on the back of your card.
Call your local cyber police cell to file a report before hanging up.
Threaten to sue the caller.
explanation: Hanging up breaks the emotional state of urgency. Verifying independently via details printed on your physical card isolates you from spoof contacts.
learningObjective: Execute safe sequences during high-pressure vishing.

questionText: What is the most robust defensive rule to protect yourself from phone-based social engineering requests?
options: Change your SIM card every month.
Never share passwords, PINs, OTPs, or biometric codes over a call, regardless of who the caller claims to be.
Use only landline connections for sensitive calls.
Never pick up calls from unknown numbers.
explanation: No legitimate financial or support institution will ever ask for passwords, PINs, or verification codes over a telephone call.
learningObjective: Apply the absolute credentials secrecy rule.

questionText: Under what circumstances does receiving money into your account require you to scan a QR code or enter your UPI PIN?
options: When the sender is from another state.
Only when the transaction exceeds ₹10,000.
NEVER. Entering your UPI PIN is strictly for authorizing payments/debts, not receiving credits.
When receiving refunds from e-commerce portals.
explanation: Entering your UPI PIN authorizes a debit from your account. Senders only need your VPA/number to pay you; they never need you to enter a PIN or scan a QR code.

questionText: A buyer on OLX/Marketplace agrees to purchase your listing. They send you a QR code claiming: "Scan this to receive your ₹5,000 payment instantly." What is the safest response?
options: Scan the QR code and enter your UPI PIN to approve the transaction.
Refuse the transaction immediately. Real buyers transfer money directly and do not send receipt QR codes.
Change your UPI PIN first, then scan the QR code.
Request them to send a credit card number instead.
explanation: Lottery/marketplace QR scams trick sellers into scanning codes that set up instant debit authorizations. Never scan QR codes to receive money.

questionText: You scan a QR code at a retail merchant. The payment app shows the name "J.K. Enterprises" but the banner on the counter reads "Mega Foodcourt". What indicator is suspicious?
options: The mismatched payment name (potential tampered QR code sticker).
The app took 5 seconds to load.
The merchant didn't smile.
The payment is made via mobile network.
explanation: Scammers paste tampered QR stickers over merchants' original codes. Always verify that the name resolved on your app screen matches the business name.

questionText: What is the utility of reviewing transaction alerts sent to your mobile phone?
options: They exist only to clutter your SMS inbox.
They allow you to verify the exact amount and merchant name being debited from your bank account.
They are sent to verify your SIM operator is active.
They allow you to claim tax deductions.
explanation: Reviewing alerts ensures that unauthorized debits are caught immediately. Check details like value, currency, and recipient before entering any authorization codes.

questionText: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023, what is the maximum prison sentence for cheating (BNS Section 318)?
options: Up to 3 years
Up to 5 years
Up to 7 years
Up to 10 years
explanation: Section 318 of BNS (formerly IPC 420) provides for imprisonment of up to 7 years and a fine for cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.
learningObjective: Identify criminal penalties for financial cheating.
